jobs.title: Product Manager - UX/UI Focus (AI x Greentech) (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
As a Product Manager at Reonic , you’ll own product problems from discovery through execution.
 You’ll work closely with customers, product, design, and engineering to understand what users need, define the right solutions, and bring them to life. A strong focus of your role will be shaping the UX and UI of our product — from improving existing workflows to designing entirely new experiences.
 You’ll combine product thinking with a strong eye for design, constantly asking: What problem are we solving, for whom, and how can we make the experience as simple and valuable as possible? 
 You’ll have significant ownership and the opportunity to directly shape how the product looks, feels, and works.
 Please note: This is a fully onsite role in Augsburg. 
 
 What you'll do 
 Own product problems end-to-end: Take ownership of product areas from discovery and problem definition through prioritization, design, development, launch, and iteration.

 Shape the user experience: Design intuitive, efficient, and delightful experiences across the product. Turn complex workflows into simple solutions that users can understand and adopt quickly.

 Understand our users: Talk to customers, analyze feedback and usage data, identify pain points, and develop a deep understanding of how renewable installers work.

 Think beyond the brief: Challenge assumptions, identify opportunities, and make sure we’re solving the right problem rather than simply building what was initially requested.

 Design and prototype: Work hands-on with wireframes, prototypes, and UI concepts to explore solutions quickly. Iterate with users and the team before investing heavily in development.

 Set the UX/UI bar: Maintain a high standard for usability, consistency, accessibility, and visual quality across the product.

 Balance user and business needs: Make thoughtful product trade-offs based on customer value, business impact, technical feasibility, and available data.

 Work closely with engineering: Collaborate with engineers throughout the product development process, communicate requirements clearly, and make pragmatic decisions when trade-offs arise.

 Iterate after launch: Treat shipping as the beginning, not the end. Measure outcomes, collect feedback, identify opportunities, and continuously improve the product experience.

 Leverage AI in your workflow: Use AI tools to accelerate research, ideation, prototyping, analysis, and product development.

 
 What Makes You a Great Fit 
 Product experience: 2+ years of experience in product management, product design, UX/UI, or a similar product-focused role, ideally in a startup or fast-growing product environment.

 Strong product sense: You naturally think about customer problems, business impact, and outcomes rather than simply features and output.

 UX/UI expertise: You have a strong understanding of interaction design, information architecture, visual design, and usability. You care deeply about how a product feels to use.

 Hands-on approach: You’re comfortable getting into Figma, creating wireframes and prototypes, testing ideas, and iterating on designs yourself.

 Customer obsession: You enjoy talking to users and can translate qualitative feedback and observed behavior into clear product opportunities.

 Comfort with ambiguity: You can take an unclear problem, structure it, identify what matters, and move towards a solution without needing every detail defined upfront.

 Strong communication: You can clearly explain product decisions, design rationale, and trade-offs to engineers, designers, leadership, and other stakeholders.

 Ownership: You take responsibility for outcomes, make decisions, and follow problems through from initial idea to measurable impact.

 Technical curiosity: You enjoy working closely with engineers and are interested in understanding the technical constraints and possibilities behind the products you build.

 AI-native mindset: You’re curious about how AI can improve both the products we build and the way we build them.

  
 Why Join Us? 
 Real impact: Help build software that enables businesses to accelerate the transition to renewable energy.

 A product people use: Our platform is already used by 3,000+ paying B2B customers , giving you the opportunity to work on a product with real users and real-world impact.

 High ownership: We’re a growing company, and nothing is set in stone. You’ll have plenty of room to shape how we work and how the product evolves.

 Fast-moving environment: Work closely with engineering and other teams, make decisions quickly, and see your work reach customers.

 A great international team: We work hard, learn from each other, and make sure we have fun along the way.

jobs.title: Product Manager - QA & Release Coordination (AI x Greentech) (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
As a Product Manager at Reonic , you’ll sit at the intersection of product, engineering, and our customers.
 You’ll help make sure new features are tested thoroughly, releases run smoothly, and customer feedback continuously makes its way back into the product development process.
 You’ll have a lot of ownership and work closely with engineers and other teams to improve both our product and the way we build and release it.
 Please note: This is a fully onsite role in Augsburg. 
 
 What you'll do 
 Own release testing: Coordinate testing for upcoming releases and continuously test new features during development. Identify issues early and provide clear, actionable feedback to engineering.

 Coordinate software releases: Keep track of features, changes, dependencies, and release timelines. Act as a communication hub between product, engineering, and other teams.

 Improve product quality: Look beyond whether a feature technically works. Think about edge cases, usability, customer workflows, and how changes affect the overall product experience.

 Turn feedback into action: Triage user feedback and bug reports, investigate issues, reproduce problems, and translate findings into clear, well-described tickets for engineering.

 Communicate what's new: Create release notes, run internal demos, and make sure colleagues understand what has changed and how new functionality works.

 Work closely with engineering: Collaborate with engineers throughout the development process, ask the right questions, and help remove ambiguity before features reach customers.

 Understand our customers: Build a deep understanding of the businesses using Reonic and use that context to make better product decisions.

 
 What Makes You a Great Fit 
 Product mindset: You naturally think beyond checklists. You want to understand why something is being built, who it is for, and what makes it useful.

 Attention to detail: You spot inconsistencies, edge cases, and potential issues before they become customer problems.

 Strong communication: You can clearly communicate with engineers, product colleagues, and other stakeholders. Professional fluency in English (C1+) is required.

 Technical curiosity: You enjoy understanding how software works and aren't afraid to dig into technical details, investigate bugs, or learn new concepts.

 Customer orientation: You care about the experience of the people using the product and can turn qualitative feedback into actionable insights.

 Ownership: You take responsibility, follow things through, and don't wait for someone else to solve a problem that you can help solve yourself.

 Startup mindset: You’re comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve and processes are still being built.

 Relevant experience: Experience in product management, product operations, QA, software development, B2B SaaS, or a similar role is a plus. A degree in economics, engineering, computer science, or a related field is also helpful, but not required.

 
 Why Join Us? 
 Real impact: Help build software that enables businesses to accelerate the transition to renewable energy.

 A product people use: Our platform is already used by 3,000+ paying B2B customers , giving you the opportunity to work on a product with real users and real-world impact.

 High ownership: We’re a growing company, and nothing is set in stone. You’ll have plenty of room to shape how we work and how the product evolves.

 Fast-moving environment: Work closely with engineering and other teams, make decisions quickly, and see your work reach customers.

 A great international team: We work hard, learn from each other, and make sure we have fun along the way.

 Great setup: MacBook, gym membership subsidy, regular team events, coffee, Deutschland ticket and other perks.

 Competitive compensation: We offer competitive pay based on your experience and responsibilities.

 
 Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply! Imposter syndrome shouldn't hold you back— we value talent and passion above all.

 At Reonic, we’re on a mission to simplify renewable technology.

jobs.title: Platform Product Manager - SAP (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
About Qorelo
 Almost every large company in the DACH region is facing the same task: the transformation to SAP S/4HANA. These programmes run for years, cost tens of millions, and regularly stall at the same point — nobody fully understands the legacy landscape that has grown over decades.
 That is where Qorelo comes in. We are building the AI layer for S/4HANA transformation: we read code, processes and documentation, make the existing landscape transparent, and deliver the fit-to-standard analysis in weeks instead of months. The knowledge stays with the customer afterwards — including in day-to-day operations, long after the system integrators have moved on.
 We've raised $3.5M from HPI Ventures, the fund tied to the institute of SAP co-founder Hasso Plattner, along with other strong backers. We already work with Fortune 500 and DAX 40 companies, including Mercedes-Benz.
 
 The role
 You'll be the person who decides what we build next, and why. You'll lead our two solution architects — the people who carry our SAP domain depth — and turn what they know about real transformation projects into a roadmap our engineers can ship. You'll work in close collaboration with our Head of Product Design and the engineering team, and you'll spend real time with the people who use the product: consultants, IT leads, and transformation teams inside enterprise clients.
 This is an early-stage PM role in the full sense: strategy and backlog, customer discovery and acceptance criteria, the big roadmap call and the unglamorous ticket. You'll do IC work alongside the thinking, and your decisions will show up in the product within weeks, running inside some of the largest SAP landscapes in Europe.
 
 What you'll own
 The product roadmap. You prioritize what our AI agents learn to do next across the transformation lifecycle — from fit-to-standard analysis to post-go-live evolution — and you can defend every call with customer evidence.

 The solution architects. You lead our two SAs directly, turning their module knowledge and project scar tissue into product requirements engineering can build against.

 Discovery with real users. Consultants and enterprise IT teams use Qorelo inside live transformation programmes. You sit with them, watch where the product wins and where it fails, and bring that back as decisions, not just notes.

 The bridge between domain and build. SAP depth on one side, an AI-native engineering team on the other. You speak enough of both languages that nothing gets lost in translation — and you work with our Head of Product Design so what we ship is usable by SAP people, not just correct.

 Shipping. Specs, acceptance criteria, tradeoffs, cut lines. Features reach real users on real landscapes, and you own whether they landed.
 

 What you need
 4+ years hands-on SAP experience, functional or product side — S/4HANA transformation, fit-to-standard, and module-level depth in at least one core area like FI, SD, or PP

 2+ years product experience: you've owned a roadmap, prioritized with engineering, and shipped features to real users — title doesn't matter, ownership does

 Understanding of the SAP transformation lifecycle (Discover → Prepare → Explore → Realize) deep enough to talk credibly to consultants and IT leads at enterprise clients

 Strong AI curiosity — you've actually built or worked with LLM/agentic tooling, not just read about it

 Comfort in an early-stage environment: ambiguity, speed, IC work alongside strategy

 Fluent English; German is a plus for our DACH client base
 

 You might be a fit if
 You've sat inside an S/4HANA programme and thought "half of this should be software" — and can name which half

 You've been the person consultants trust on module questions and the person engineers trust to write a clear spec

 You've built something with LLMs — a prototype, an internal tool, an agent — and formed opinions about where they break

 You want your product decisions to run inside DAX 40 landscapes within weeks, not sit in a committee for quarters
 

 What we offer
 Real ownership. Meaningful equity and a direct hand in the company's direction, not just your backlog. We're looking for people who want to shape a company, not join one.

 Competitive salary , benchmarked for senior product talent in Berlin.

 The problems. Fortune 500 and DAX 40 production landscapes, including Mercedes-Benz. Your roadmap decisions run at the core of companies most PMs only read about.

 The team. Short paths, fast decisions, and a direct line to the engineers and architects who build what you define.

 Company offsites with the whole team.

 The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running

 4+ years of product management experience, with meaningful time spent on identity verification, KYC/AML, fraud, or authentication/security products.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager - Carpool Experience
jobs.description:
About BlaBlaCar 

 BlaBlaCar is the world’s leading community-based travel app enabling 27 million members a year to carpool or travel by bus in 21 countries. Our team of 800 employees counts over 50 nationalities and is spread across our 5 global offices, 30% working fully remotely. 
 

 The role 

 Carpool Experience covers everything between two members once they have found each other: agreeing on the trip, talking, meeting up, and building trust.

 Vision: a carpool experience that feels easy and safe for passengers and drivers, from the first hello to the final goodbye.

 Mission: make it simple for members to talk, negotiate, meet up and trust each other.

 You own six product areas, used by millions of members every month:

 
 
 Negotiation. Before booking, passengers can ask the driver for a detour, a lower price or another special request, and add a tip. Drivers accept, decline or make a counter-offer. It launched in France in 2025 and went worldwide in 2026. It is still a new product: what it should become, and how far it can go, is yours to figure out.

 
 Messaging. The chat between drivers and passengers. Next up: Group Chat, and catching up with market standards.

 
 GPS Tracking: both the technical capability as well as features it enables (including sharing ETA on the map, ESC bonus in Spain among others)

 
 Post-Carpool ride XP (claims, ratings etc.). How members build trust in each other. This includes AI Ratings Summary, BlaBlaCar's first consumer-facing GenAI feature.

 
 Communication Service and contact preferences. The platform that sends every push notification, email, SMS and WhatsApp message across the company, plus the settings members use to choose what they receive.

 
 Marketing tools. Braze and deeplinks, used by the CRM and marketing teams.

 
 This is a key scope, and you own its strategy. That comes with high exposure: you present to the Executive Committee every two weeks. You get a direct say in company decisions, and you are expected to bring clear thinking and solid arguments to the table.

 Your Responsibilities 

 Set the direction. Build the vision and strategy for your scope, turn it into ambitious OKRs, and get leadership behind them.

 Own the numbers. Know your business metrics, reliability targets and costs in detail. Review them every month and act on what they tell you, without being asked.

 Shape the future of Negotiation. Work out where its real value is for members and for BlaBlaCar, decide how it should evolve (new use cases such as negotiation after booking, conversion, usage), and prove the impact on passengers (PAX) and GMV.

 Ship the next member interactions: Group Chat, live location for both drivers and passengers, and the next version of the Communication Service.

 Run experiments and rollouts with discipline. Run A/B tests and country-by-country launches with decision rules set in advance, together with Legal, Privacy and country leads.

 Hold your own with the ExCo. Every two weeks, present progress, decisions and trade-offs to the Executive Committee. Take a clear position, defend it, and change it when the evidence calls for it.

Project Q GmbH ("Q") is a defence technology company with offices in Berlin and Munich, and a trusted partner of the German Armed Forces. Our customers field sensors, drones and C2 systems from many vendors that were never built to work together. We build Hydris, an orchestration layer that integrates the systems they already field, and the ones they'll add next, into one picture operators can act on across defence, public safety, and critical infrastructure. Hydris runs at the edge, keeps working when the link drops, and its core is open source under Apache 2.0.

As Senior Product Manager for Mission Devices, you'll own the hardware that puts Hydris in the field. 

You'll work end-to-end, from discovery with operators through hardware build cycles to fielded units, and you'll decide what gets built rather than work through someone else's backlog. The bar is concrete: devices that run for months off-grid in contested RF environments.

What you'll do
 Discovery and requirements Spend time with end users in their operating environment to understand their workflows in depth, not just their stated requirements.
 Validate assumptions about value, usability, feasibility and viability through prototypes, bench tests and field trials before committing to hardware fabrication.
 Analyze contractual specifications with Program Managers, separating firm constraints from areas where there's room for the best technical solution.
 Roadmap and delivery Maintain an outcome-focused roadmap aligned to hardware build cycles (EVT/DVT/PVT), firmware releases and OTA update pipelines.
 Define requirements and field metrics for each device, including detection performance, energy efficiency, mission endurance and SWaP, and make the trade-offs between them.
 Prioritize investment across the device family, deciding where to extend existing devices and where a new one is needed.
 Systems and interoperability Make sure devices integrate with Hydris as and interoperate with third-party systems through industry standards and protocols.
 Design provisioning, commissioning and deployment workflows that are simple and reliable in the field.
 Investigate issues that span hardware, firmware and communications, and work with engineering to resolve them.
 Collaboration Act as the main source of product context and the product's champion, making sure the team, leadership and customers understand what we're building and why.
 Work in a product trio with engineering (hardware and ML) and design. 
 Partner with Program and Capture Managers to keep the product vision aligned with contractual commitments.
 Write clear PRDs and decision records, and mentor teammates on discovery practice and hardware–software trade-offs.
 
You should apply if you have
 5+ years of product management experience with hardware–software products, for example in embedded systems, IoT, robotics, defence systems or edge AI.
 Experience taking a connected hardware product from EVT/DVT through production into operational use, including in-field updates.
 Experience running product development end to end, from discovery to engineering-ready work, and the ability to adapt to however a team works.
 Ability making decisions with incomplete information, and the judgment to know when a decision is risky enough to slow down.
 Clear communication with hardware engineers, ML researchers and operators alike.
 Motivation to contribute to European security and sovereignty.
 Willingness to travel regularly to military exercises, test ranges and customer sites in Germany and NATO partner countries, sometimes in demanding field conditions.
 Eligibility for German security clearance (SÜ2).
 Fluency in German and English (C1 or higher).
 You'd be a particularly great fit with 
 A degree in electrical, mechanical or systems engineering, robotics or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience bringing hardware products from prototype to production.
 Experience in military, public safety or other mission-critical operational environments.
 Exposure to sensor fusion, mesh networking or degraded RF environments, including familiarity with interoperability standards such as Cursor on Target, SAPIENT, ONVIF or ASTERIX.

We're on a mission 
 Every business grows through a CRM and a direct line to its customers. Healthcare, and pharmacy most of all, is the one place that never happened. It was too hard to build, too hard to distribute, and too hard to do compliantly. Customer data sits idle whilst running a community healthcare business continues to become structurally tighter.
  
 We're on a mission to change that. We are the compliant data layer for community healthcare: the system that lets a pharmacy use the patient data it already holds to grow revenue and relationships, compliantly, on the clinical system it already runs.
  
 This is already working. Pharmlogic is NHS-assured, integrated and lives in hundreds of pharmacies nationwide, and we've powered millions of patient communications.
  
 The role 
 You will run marketing across the board: brand and social, the website, copy across everything we put out, how we explain the product, and the campaigns that keep our pharmacy customers engaged. You own the channels and you set the standard for how Pharmlogic sounds and looks.
  
 You report to the CEO and work closely with the founding team. This is a hands-on role for a generalist who can write, ship, and run several channels at once without waiting to be told. You are early, and the function is yours to shape.
  
 The problems you'll own 
  
 Carrying the message: Take our vision, the why behind Pharmlogic, and make it land with the people we exist for. You translate what we believe into words that busy healthcare teams trust and can act on.

 Communicating in a regulated space: Everything we put out can be read by healthcare professionals, other stakeholders and by patients. You write with the clarity, accuracy and care that demands, where compliant and compelling are the same standard, not a trade-off.

 Our voice, everywhere: Own how Pharmlogic sounds across social, the website, campaigns and the product itself. One voice, centred on the vision, consistent wherever someone meets us.

 From product to message: Turn what we build into messaging tailored to all stakeholders in a busy healthcare team that can be immediately understood. You make the complex simple without sacrificing value.

 The customer journey: Own the communications that take a pharmacy from signed to thriving, engaged, getting full value, and staying, so the story we tell is the experience they have.

 Knowing what works: Measure what you put out, double down on what performs, and feed what you learn back into how we market, sell and build.

 Pharmlogic in the room: with the team at sector events, from the stand and the materials to the follow-up, so the people we meet in person get the same clear story as everyone else, and conversations turn into pipeline.

  
 This could be for you if 
  
 You're an excellent communicator, above all. Writing is the craft at the centre of this job. You make complex things simple without making them shallow, you have taste, and it shows in everything you put out.

 You've done lifecycle and product marketing in high-pace SaaS. You know how to take what a product does and turn it into a message people act on, and how to run the journey from signed customer to engaged advocate. That experience is what lets you move fast here from day one.

 You thrive on the team's success. You get more from a customer win or a teammate's great launch than from your own byline. Small team, shared scoreboard.

 You share the vision. You believe every healthcare business should be able to understand its customers and improve care for them while staying viable. If that sentence resonates rather than reads as marketing, this will feel like your work, not just a job.

 You ship at startup pace. You put things out, learn, and go again, rather than polishing one thing for a month, and you do it without waiting for a brief.

 Tooling fluency helps. Comfort with a CMS, email platforms, CRMs and basic design is a real advantage.

jobs.title: Technical Project Manager - France
jobs.description:
Build something monumental for Healthcare!

 
 At Tandem Health we’re reimagining healthcare by putting clinicians first. Our platform - designed by clinicians, for clinicians - is built on deep insight into real-world pain points, with intuitive medical notes and workflows that truly support patient care.
 We’re a fast-scaling health-tech company backed by top investors and expanding globally. We move fast, stay curious, and believe building something that matters starts with an extraordinary team. If you're passionate about impact and innovation, we'd love to meet you!
 
 About the Role 
 You care about making complex systems actually work, not just in theory, but in practice - across teams, stakeholders, and real-world constraints. In previous roles, you were likely the person who brought clarity to messy situations: aligning engineers, partners, and product teams to get things shipped.

At Tandem, you'll drive how our platform connects with the external systems used across French and European healthcare - owning and driving some of the most critical technical initiatives we have. You'll be based in our France office, working alongside the local team, in close collaboration with our central Integrations team in Stockholm. A big part of the role is deeply understanding both sides: the capabilities and constraints of external systems, and those of our own platform. From that understanding, you'll find ways to integrate them and shape concrete proposals for how integrations should work, together with external partners.

You move fast, but not carelessly. You know how to break down complex problems, prioritize what matters, and keep momentum across multiple workstreams. You're comfortable going deep technically when needed, understanding APIs, data flows, and system constraints, while still keeping the bigger product picture in mind.
 
This is a high-impact role where you'll not only deliver projects, but shape how we build and scale technical products at Tandem.
 
 What You'll Do 
 Lead integration work with external partners and healthcare systems, ensuring high-quality, scalable implementations.

 Map external systems against our own platform and propose concrete integration designs to external partners.

 Act as the central point of coordination between engineering, partnerships, and external stakeholders, bridging the local team in France and the integrations team in Stockholm.

 Translate complex technical requirements into clear priorities, plans, and deliverables.

 Work closely with engineers to understand APIs, data models, and system architecture, and ensure solutions are robust and aligned with our platform.

 Identify bottlenecks, manage dependencies, and keep projects moving at high velocity.

 Build and improve how we work - establishing processes, templates, and frameworks for integrations and technical delivery.

 Ensure strong visibility across stakeholders - tracking progress, surfacing risks, and communicating clearly.

 Support our sales organisation in answering technical questions from our customers.
 

 What You Bring 
 Experience as a Technical Project Manager or similar role in a SaaS, platform, or healthtech environment.

 Strong ability to drive complex, cross-functional initiatives involving both internal teams and external stakeholders.

 Technical fluency - comfortable discussing APIs, authentication, integrations, and system design with engineers.

 Proven ability to manage multiple workstreams without losing clarity or momentum.

 Ability to anticipate, assess, and manage risk in projects, from scoping through to delivery.

 Strong communication skills, you can translate technical complexity into clear decisions and direction.

 A product mindset - you care about building the right thing, not just delivering on time.

 Native level french speaking.

 Bonus Points 
 Experience in tech sales, enterprise sales, or enterprise software delivery

 Experience working with healthcare systems or regulated environments

 Familiarity with FHIR, HL7, or other healthcare data standards

 Experience working with platform or API products

 Some hands-on technical experience (e.g. scripting, debugging, light coding)

 Experience scaling integration processes or working with multiple external partners

 
 Location 
 We believe the best ideas happen when we're together. This role is based in our Paris office, where you will work primarily on-site with the local team, while collaborating closely with colleagues at our HQ in Stockholm.
 
 How to Apply 
 We adopt a continuous selection process, so please make sure to apply with your CV in English.

Our interview process consists of 4 stages:
 Screening interview with Talent Acquisition

 Technical interview with some of our Engineering team

 Follow-up interview with one of our Team Leads

 Home case and presentation at our Paris office - Join us for a lunch, a discovery meeting and a presentation to experience our culture firsthand, collaborate

 About Netholabs
 Netholabs builds large-scale neural and behavioural recording platforms to generate the data needed for the next generation of brain models. We operate two recording platforms: a preclinical ethological monitoring system integrated with behaviour and neural data and a human motion-capture and neurophysiology platform. We are a small, fast-moving team where hardware, neuroscience, and ML sit in the same room.
  
 The Role
 We are building integrated human motion-capture and neurophysiological recording systems for both controlled lab studies and naturalistic, in-the-wild data collection. Today we have working prototypes. We need someone to turn them into products - reproducible, manufacturable, remotely updatable systems that can be deployed at scale and maintained without an engineer in the room.
 You will own R&D delivery across the London lab and hardware programme: co-developing the hardware with our electronics and mechanical engineers, importing and enforcing best-practice data capture protocols, and engaging contract manufacturers to scale. This is an agentic, hands-on role -with support engineer roles as required. You will spend as much time in the lab and on the phone with suppliers as you will in a spec document.
  
 What you'll do
 Take working prototypes to shippable, field-deployable systems — define the product, own the roadmap, and drive it to delivery

 Specify and build out over-the-air update infrastructure: firmware, versioning, rollback, fleet management, remote diagnostics

 Own the design-for-manufacture transition — DFM/DFA reviews, BOM ownership, tolerancing, test fixtures, and production test protocols

 Identify, qualify, and manage contract manufacturers and suppliers; own the relationship from RFQ through NPI to sustained production

 Establish and enforce best-practice data capture protocols across modalities (EEG, fNIRS, EMG, pupillometry, motion capture, video) so that data quality is consistent across sessions, operators, and sites

 Define the requirements that make in-the-wild collection viable: wearability, session setup time, robustness, battery life, and unattended operation

 Work directly with our electronics, mechanical, firmware, and neuroscience teams to translate research needs into hardware requirements — and push back when a requirement doesn't survive contact with manufacturing

 Build the quality, documentation, and regulatory groundwork (design history, ISO 13485-style discipline, CE/UKCA pathway) appropriate to a research-device product

 Contribute to the industrialisation of our rodent recording platform where the manufacturing and OTA problems overlap
  

 What we're looking for
 Essential
 Min 3+ years (ideal 7+) in hardware product management, product engineering, or programme management, with several products you personally took from prototype to volume manufacture 

 Direct, demonstrable experience with contract manufacturers: you have run RFQs, sat through NPI builds, argued about yield, and fixed a production line problem from 6,000 miles away

 Deep understanding of connected-device architecture: OTA update mechanisms, device provisioning, telemetry, fleet management, and what it costs to get these wrong

 Fluency across electronics, mechanical, and firmware enough to hold a real technical conversation with each - you don't need to design the board, but you need to know when the answer you're getting is wrong

 Track record of writing specifications and protocols that people actually follow

 Comfort with ambiguity and a small-company reality: no PMO, no roadmap tooling team, no one to delegate the boring parts to

 Strongly preferred 
 Experience with wearable, biosignal, or medical device hardware

 Familiarity with human research data collection — protocols, participant handling, IRB/ethics, GDPR and special-category data

 Experience shipping a product to CE/UKCA or FDA pathway

 Background in neuroscience, biomedical engineering, or a related field

 Experience with multi-sensor time synchronisation and the data infrastructure behind it

 What we offer
 Direct ownership of a product line at a company small enough that your decisions ship

 Equity in an early-stage company building foundational infrastructure for brain modelling

 A team of neuroscientists and engineers doing genuinely novel work

 Central London lab, on-site, with access to the Sussex rodent facility

Le poste

Rejoignez une équipe qui façonne l’avenir de l’industrie grâce à l’IA. En tant que Value & Adoption Lead, votre mission principale sera de pérenniser l’appropriation des solutions Cognite au sein de nos comptes stratégiques les plus complexes.

Avec des milliers d’utilisateurs actifs sur le terrain, des installations industrielles multiples et des produits de données en production, nos partenariats de co-innovation majeurs s'inscrivent dans des transformations de l'IA sur plusieurs années.

Dans ce rôle, vous ferez le pont entre le déploiement technique et la concrétisation de la valeur métier. En étroite collaboration avec les clients et l'équipe des comptes stratégiques, vous pilotez de bout en bout l’intégration de nos technologies — telles que l’IA agentique, Flows et Adaptive Expériences — dans le quotidien opérationnel des ingénieurs sur site, des planificateurs de maintenance et des équipes de direction.

Concevoir des parcours ciblés via Cognite Academy, mettre en place des formations de formateurs et encadrer les phases de transition vers un support renforcé.
  • Fédérer un réseau de référents internes : Identifier, mobiliser et former les relais d’opinion et utilisateurs clés sur chaque site pour assurer l'autonomie à long terme du client.

Coordonner les équipes transverses — Delivery, ingénierie terrain, Academy et Customer Success — pour lever rapidement ces obstacles.

jobs.title: Founding Product Manager
jobs.description:
Hi, we're Dana and Erik, the founders of Circonomit. We build the decision platform industrial companies use to plan their production.
 Dana sees the customer side. She needs to know which use cases we can sell today, which we cannot, and what a demo is allowed to claim.
 Erik sees the engineering side. He needs requirements that are ready to be built, complete, and clear about what we deliberately leave out.
 The product sits between the two, and that is this role. We sell vertically, one use case at a time, while the product has to stay general enough to serve the next customer without being rebuilt. You decide what we build next, in which order, and what we decline.
 How you will be measured: how much of today's project work is standard product a year from now, and how quickly a recognised customer problem becomes a usable capability.
 We came out of RWTH research, raised €2.8M with Vorwerk Ventures, and have customers running on our models today. Small team, Cologne office.
 Requirements 
 5+ years in product management, or consulting with genuine product proximity. You have owned a product area end to end, not only a backlog.
 A technical and analytical foundation: engineering, data, operations research, quantitative controlling, or finance with real modelling.
 You recognise when a requirement creates technical debt or will not be reusable at the next customer. You will not write production code.
 Experience deciding under incomplete information, and explaining the trade-offs afterwards: what you chose, why, and what it cost.
 You are comfortable working directly with plant managers and controllers, and understand how they decide today.
 German at C1 level or above, and fluent English. Customer conversations happen in German.
 Existing work visa for Germany.
 You should enjoy being in front of customers in your first week, and deciding without a research team behind you. Priorities change as we learn from customers, and we make scope and trade-offs explicit together.
 Benefits 
 Ownership. The roadmap, and where the line between product and customer project sits.
 Shaping the role. This is the founding product role. You define how product works here: discovery, prioritisation, and the standards between product and engineering.
 Exposure. You present your roadmap and the reasoning behind it to the board, and you sit in the core strategy conversations.
 Real-world impact. Customers plan their production on our models today.
 Direct collaboration. Small team, no org chart. We work directly together. Weekly feedback, both ways.
 Compensation. Competitive salary plus a VSOP package reflecting your contribution and development in the role.
 Hybrid work. Our HQ is in Cologne, and we meet there regularly.
 Your setup and everyday extras. Hardware of your choice · AI tooling budget · sports membership · Deutschland-Ticket.
 Process: An intro call, a second conversation with the team, a 60- to 90-minute live case on a real customer requirement, then in-person conversations with the team.

jobs.title: Product Marketing Manager in Legal Tech (Zurich)
jobs.description:
Description Legal AI content is turning into a commodity. Every vendor ships the same AI-generated blog posts and the same generic battlecards. We are transitioning into an AI-native company ourselves, and that changes what this role has to be. You would sit in the marketing department with a dotted line to the product department, but not as a traditional product marketer who ships a few blog posts and calls it enablement. Not as a pure thinker who never touches a sales deck. Instead, as one person who owns our voice and turns it into everything the company needs to win: the thesis that gets us cited, the sales slide that closes next week’s deal, and the briefing that gets a General Counsel to say yes. 
 You will use AI tooling and agents to cover ground that used to take a small team, so you can spend your own time on the part that cannot be delegated: the thinking, the judgment, and the writing that actually changes someone’s mind. 

 Your mission 1. Product Marketing & Market Intelligence  
 Drive go-to-market impact for launches and expansion, from plan to execution. 

 Own deep knowledge of our ICP and competitive landscape, and feed it back into the product and sales strategy. 

 Bring market and customer truth back to Product so we build what actually matters. 

 Work across Product, Marketing, Sales and leadership. You don’t sit in a silo. 

 2. Positioning, Narrative & Thought Leadership  
 Own positioning: define what Legartis stands for, against which alternatives, for which buyer. 

 Develop and defend clear, evidence-backed points of view on where Legal AI is going. Not generic AI-created opinions, but real positions based on customer and buyer research (interviews with General Counsel, CFOs, legal operations leaders). 

 Conceive flagship studies and thought leadership content. Direct AI tools to help you scale production while you own the substance and the voice.

jobs.description:
Who we are 
 
 Yubo is the Social Discovery app to make new friends and hang out online. By eliminating likes and follows, we empower our users to create genuine connections and show up as their true selves.
 
 We've pioneered a new way for Gen Z to socialize online, and with millions of active users, our goal is to redefine how we connect today and tomorrow.
 
 Our team is international, multicultural and deeply committed to its mission. As the leading platform to socialize online, we have a special responsibility to build a safe digital space for our community. Safety is embedded in our DNA, and our proactive approach focuses on user protection, support, and education.
 
 Join us in this exciting journey and help us shape the future of social interactions!

At Yubo, Product Managers have real ownership. They work in strong partnership with Product Designers and Engineering, shaping strategy and decisions from problem definition all the way to delivery, with direct and visible impact on both the product and the business.
 We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to form that partnership with a Product Designer: a duo jointly responsible for the end-to-end experiences you ship together. You'll take ownership of a strategic product area, identify the biggest opportunities, and turn them into clear product bets on a product used by millions of people.
 We're moving away from small, isolated feature launches toward bigger, end-to-end experiences tested at scale . You'll combine user understanding, data and strong product convictions to frame problems, shape solutions with Design and Engineering, and decide what to scale, iterate, or stop.
 You'll also work closely with Data, Machine Learning, Brand Marketing and Trust & Safety on challenges ranging from recommendation and discovery to retention, safety, monetization and AI.

 To make this dream duo work, we’re basing this role in Paris and looking for someone willing to come to the office once or twice a week.

 Own a strategic product area from problem definition through delivery and post-launch iteration

 You combine strong product intuition with analytical rigor

 You know how to use data, research, user feedback, and experimentation to guide decisions

 You start with the user problem rather than jumping straight to a feature or solution

 You enjoy working closely with Design and Engineering and leading through influence rather than hierarchy

 You are comfortable making decisions with imperfect information and changing direction when the evidence tells you to

 You know how to balance user experience with growth, engagement, monetization, safety, and long-term product health

 Experience with social, community, social discovery, gaming, recommendation, or consumer subscription products is a plus

jobs.title: Senior Growth Product Manager AI Native
jobs.description:
About Magic Eden and Dicey 
Magic Eden reached unicorn status in just 9 months after launch, one of the fastest in history. We built a category-defining NFT marketplace from scratch and proved we know how to move fast. Now we're doing it again. Dicey is our crypto casino and sportsbook platform, targeting the $180B+ iGaming and sports betting markets.
 We're a small, fully remote team. We ship fast, we're hands-on with our data, and we're rebuilding how a growth team operates around AI from the ground up.
 The role 
Most of the iGaming industry competes on acquisition. Almost nobody has figured out personalized retention, knowing who a player is, what they need right now, and what would actually change their behavior this week. That's the problem you'll own.
 This role focuses on the full post-signup journey: expanding our player segmentation framework, designing and running targeted offers and campaigns, and owning the P&L lever that comes with it. It's explicitly AI-native. You'll build workflows, agents, and pipelines to run lifecycle campaigns that would have taken a whole team two years ago. Half the job is identifying the right problem. The other half is running the experiments to find the answer.
 What you'll do 
 Own retention and monetization as a growth loop. Set the targets, find the leverage, and drive the numbers for everything that happens after a player signs up

 Own the player segmentation framework. Today it's value and risk. You decide how it evolves, what signals feed it, and how the rest of the company uses it

 Build the AI-native growth stack. Analysis, agents, and automated pipelines that surface segments, generate offer candidates, and run campaigns with minimal manual work

 Design and ship targeted offers for specific segments and moments: reload bonuses, lossback, wager bounties, challenges, win-back sequences. Size them, spec them, ship them, measure them

 Spend real time in our data warehouse and on-chain data finding patterns and turn them into campaigns before anyone else does

 Expand the signals we have on players: on-chain activity, status-match programs, social account linking, and whatever else you can think of

 Run the campaigns. Email, in-app, Telegram, whatever the channel. You're hands-on with it, with AI doing the heavy lifting

 Partner with engineering and design to ship the product surfaces that make all of this repeatable

 What we're looking for 
 Strong intuition for player psychology and incentive design. Experience in gambling, gaming, fintech, or consumer marketplaces helps. Genuine curiosity about why people behave the way they do is required

 Deeply analytical. You can go from a vague question to a clean cohort cut yourself, without waiting on a data scientist

 AI-native by default. You already use AI to write queries, build analyses, and automate your own work and you want to push that much further

 High output with good judgment. You generate a lot of ideas and know which ones are worth testing first

 Bias to do it yourself. You're comfortable sending the email, running the query, and writing the spec, not just briefing others

 Comfortable with ambiguity. There's no playbook here, you'll be building it

 Backgrounds that tend to fit 
 Growth PM at a data-heavy consumer company

 MBB consultant who wants to move into product and own outcomes, not just advise on them

 Product Minded Data scientist or analyst who wants to ship, not just report

 Why this is interesting 
 Competitive, top-of-market compensation

 You're defining what a growth PM looks like in an AI-native company, there's no inherited playbook

 Personalised retention is where the industry is going and we're building it early

 Real ownership: a segmentation framework, a product surface, and a P&L lever, with a direct line to the founding team

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager (Business Applications Development)
jobs.description:
Are you looking to own the customer-facing experience for JetBrains products, from how individuals and organizations buy and manage software to how licensing and entitlements work behind the scenes?

About JetBrains

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

What you’ll do

In this role, you’ll lead the strategy for BAD (Business Application Development) Product. You’ll tackle the complex web of purchases, subscriptions, organization administration, and usage-based services, making sure our customers have a smooth, coherent experience every step of the way.

You’ll work closely with engineering, design, analytics, QA, and BAD Platform, as well as Sales, Customer Success, and Finance teams. You’ll have the autonomy to drive product discovery, validate hypotheses through data and experimentation, and define the long-term vision for our licensing and administration ecosystem.

Day to day, you will:

  • Define and execute the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for BAD Product systems.
  • Uncover user friction through customer research, support data, telemetry, and feedback from internal teams.
  • Map and improve end-to-end customer journeys covering purchasing, subscriptions, licensing, and administration.
  • Identify gaps, overlaps, and inconsistencies across sub-systems to build a clear, unified user experience.
  • Partner with engineering, design, analytics, and QA from early discovery through launch and continuous iteration.
  • Define and track key product metrics for adoption, conversion, and support demand.
  • Communicate product direction, trade-offs, and progress clearly to cross-functional stakeholders.

What you’ll bring

  • An ownership mindset, taking responsibility for outcomes, not just task completion.
  • A clear focus on underlying problems and desired outcomes rather than immediate feature requests.
  • Comfort with technical complexity, trade-offs, and systems thinking.
  • A preference for quality, long-term sustainability, and user trust over short-term fixes.
  • The ability to make grounded decisions using customer research, analytics, and experimentation.
  • Strong collaboration skills across multi-disciplinary teams and distinct business areas.

What you’ll need

  • A proven track record of managing technically complex SaaS, enterprise, or B2B product areas end to end.
  • Hands-on experience driving product discovery, user research, and roadmap prioritization.
  • Experience navigating complex customer journeys, multi-team dependencies, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Experience making data-informed decisions using telemetry, product metrics, and experimentation.
  • The ability to work comfortably alongside engineering teams on technical details, APIs, data models, and system integrations.
  • Fluency in English.

What success looks like

In practice, success means building a licensing and administration experience that feels seamless to the user and resilient under the hood. You'll bring clarity to ambiguous systems, simplify fragmented customer flows, and establish reliable product metrics. Ultimately, you succeed by removing friction for millions of developers and admins, allowing them to focus on their actual work.

Why join JetBrains?

  • Strong base salary – We offer competitive pay that reflects your skills and experience.
  • Flexible work schedule – Enjoy the freedom to work from home or from the office.
  • Extra time off – More days to relax, recharge, and do the things you love.
  • Learning and development opportunities – Access to conferences, courses, and language classes.
  • Relocation support – Assistance to help make your move as smooth and stress-free as possible.
  • Free meals and snacks – Lunch and refreshments provided to keep you fueled.
  • Health and wellness – On-site gyms or sports club stipends.
  • Internal events – Company-wide celebrations and team gatherings.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We know great ideas can come from anyone, anywhere. That’s why we do our best to create an open and inclusive workplace – one that welcomes everyone regardless of their background, identity, religion, age, accessibility needs, or orientation.

If this sounds like you, we’d love to read your application.

*Some benefits may vary depending on location.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Mobile
jobs.description:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser, and Pocket, a service for keeping up with the best content online. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders - only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. 

About this team and role:

We’re looking for a hands-on Mobile Product Manager with a primary focus on Firefox for iOS, while also contributing across mobile (including Android).

This role is about building a better browser, turning downloads into loyal users, and creating experiences that truly stand out. If you’ve shipped mobile apps, obsess over details that improve everyday use, and love turning user insights into real improvements, this is a great opportunity to drive impact at Firefox.

From our Macquarie Park office, we’re looking for an experienced Senior Project Manager to lead complex, high-impact software implementation projects for our customers.

You’ll shape the project approach, lead cross-functional teams, work closely with senior customer stakeholders and maintain oversight of scope, budget, quality and risk.

jobs.title: Product Manager II - Financial Crime Operations
jobs.description:
Building the Future of Open Finance 

 Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.
 
Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.
 The team 
 Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.
  
 Kraken's Compliance Operations teams, including the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), investigations and enhanced due diligence, are the front line of how Kraken detects and responds to financial crime. The systems they run on sit within Core Services Product, alongside the engineering teams who build them. That covers alert ingestion, case management, investigator tooling and a growing set of automation and AI tools.
 
 This role owns the product for that investigation platform. That means how an alert is created, enriched, grouped and suppressed. How it becomes a case. How an investigator reaches and documents a decision. And how every step is evidenced to a regulator or auditor. You'll start with the FIU, where the workflows are most complex and the audit bar is highest, then extend the platform across Compliance Operations.
  
 The opportunity 
 Own the investigation-platform roadmap end to end. Sequence it and defend it, and re-sequence it when a regulator or the RCO raises a P0.

 Define "done" before build starts. Write phased deliverables and acceptance criteria that Compliance signs off, and hold the line when scope moves.

 Get requirements in before engineering starts. Build the intake between Compliance policy, monitoring rules and case management so that changes don't reach investigators before their workflows are ready.

 Understand the process before building. Reconcile policy and SOPs against what investigators actually do and what the system actually does. Know the difference between a process fix and a technical one, and say which requests are in scope for engineering.

 Understand the pipeline well enough to challenge it: ingestion, profile and transaction resolution, suppression and grouping logic, and reconciliation between vendor output and case management. Be able to walk an auditor through it with live examples.

 Make auditability a first-class requirement: audit trail, data lineage, evidence retention, reviewer attribution, change-management controls, and validation of filtering and suppression logic.

 Ship automation and AI into regulated workflows with controls that hold up in Compliance, IT and privacy audits. That means human-in-the-loop design, explainability and ongoing monitoring.

 Run the operating rhythm: a shared forum with engineering and adjacent product managers, a regular stakeholder update, and one delivery status that everyone reads the same way.

  
 What you bring 
 4+ years of product management, including 2+ years on financial-crime systems such as transaction monitoring, investigations, case management, KYC/EDD or sanctions screening.

 Working knowledge of how an AML programme is examined, including the questions regulators, internal audit and model validation ask about monitoring, filing and control systems.

 The technical fluency to go deep on data flows and system design with engineers, and to spot when a design won't meet the requirement.

 A track record of shipping internal tools or operational platforms that measurably changed how an operations team works.

 Clear, concise writing, from PRDs and phase plans to audit walkthroughs and executive updates.

 The judgement to tell a senior stakeholder a timeline isn't realistic because the requirements aren't written yet, and to keep the relationship intact.

  
  
 Nice to haves 
 Direct FIU experience, such as alert disposition, SAR/STR filing or leading investigators.

 Crypto or digital-asset experience, such as blockchain analytics, wallet-level transaction analysis or focal vs counterparty logic.

 Experience shipping AI or ML into a regulated investigative workflow, including the control design.

 Build-vs-buy and vendor evaluation for monitoring or case-management tooling.

 Experience with programmes that span jurisdictions (UK, EU/MiCA, US).

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, Inference
jobs.description:
About Mistral 
 Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.
 We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.
 
 The role 
 Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud. Our inference platform already serves production traffic at scale. We are hiring a Lead Product Manager to own the inference portfolio within our Cloud & Inference organization.
 You'll set strategy, write specs, sit with customers running production traffic, and work across our inference, infrastructure, and go-to-market teams to deliver real customer impact. Example problems you may work on include figuring out the next inference product we should launch to help our customers scale their AI workloads or how we cut fraudulent free-tier usage without adding friction for legitimate users.
 You will work on state of the art infrastructure, in close collaboration with our science and research engineering teams. Your job is to turn that infrastructure into products that AI-native startups and enterprises pay for, integrated with our developer platform Studio.
 You will operate as an individual contributor first — taking end-to-end ownership of complex and significant product lines — while building the foundation for the inference PM team as the portfolio grows. The size and shape of the team reporting into the role will be defined together with the VP Product once you're in place; from day one the expectation is hands-on product leadership, not people management.
 You will be the first PM fully dedicated to inference and the most senior product hire in the space. You will report to the VP Product - Cloud & Inference, and work day-to-day with our inference engineering teams in the US and Europe.
 
 What you'll do 
 Strategy and vision: define the vision, strategy, and annual goals for the inference portfolio, aligned with customer needs and company objectives. Benchmark the managed-inference field and pick where we win.

 Roadmap and execution: own the full lifecycle for serverless inference, dedicated endpoints, and adjacent services. Prioritize, ship, measure, iterate. Economics: own adoption, revenue contribution, and gross margin for your products. Treat cost-per-token, unit economics, and capacity tradeoffs as product decisions, and partner with GTM, Finance and Marketing on pricing, packaging, and launches.

 Customers: spend real time with AI-native startups and enterprises running advanced production workloads. Turn their constraints, like latency, throughput, compliance, and cost, into roadmap choices.

 Engineering partnership: work daily with inference engineering and the cloud infrastructure teams behind our data centers on capacity planning, scheduling, routing, and reliability.

 Research and open source: track open-source inference advances and emerging model architectures, and turn them into performance and efficiency gains for the product.

 Team building: as the portfolio scales, help shape and grow the inference PM team — hiring, mentoring, and setting the product bar.

 
 What we're looking for 
 Deep product experience in tech and infrastructure with a track record of bringing inference, cloud infrastructure, or large-scale distributed systems to market. You have built robust, at-scale AI infrastructure first-hand.

 An engineering background before moving into product management.

 You have taken an infra or inference product from early stage to material revenue and adoption, owning complex and significant product lines end to end.

 Player-coach disposition: you lead from the front — hands-on product work now, with the range and appetite to build and coach a team as we scale.

 Fluency in the economics of the business: gross margin, unit economics, and the tradeoffs behind token pricing and GPU capacity.

 High ownership and a strong bias for action. You prototype with AI coding tools, write your own specs, and unblock yourself without waiting for engineers or designers.

 Low ego, comfort in ambiguity, and credibility with executives, engineers, and customers alike.

 
 What We Offer 
 We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. jobs.title: Founding Technical Project Manager
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 
 Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 
 Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 
 To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 
 BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 
 Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 
 
 
 Location 
 This is a full-time position based in Munich or Cologne. Following a comprehensive onboarding period at our HQ in central Zurich (minimum one month), you will work from your home location, with regular visits to customers across the DACH region.
 Team collaboration matters a lot to us. You will regularly spend time with the team in person, in Zurich and at our hubs, for team days, all-hands and offsites. These visits are financially supported by blp.
 Your Mission 
 On our largest global rollouts, connectivity is what makes or breaks the program.
 These customers run several ERP systems across many entities and countries, with interfaces, master data and process variants that have grown over decades. Whether blp is usable on day one, and whether the first go-live holds its date, depends more on getting that landscape right than on almost anything else. You are the person who makes sure it is right. You sit opposite the customer's enterprise architects and IT leads, understand what their landscape actually does rather than what the documentation says, and shape the technical solution with them.
 Getting this right is relentless project management as much as architecture. Requirements on a landscape this size never arrive clear. You chase them until they are: pushing the customer's IT organization for answers, going back when an answer is vague, and refusing to let an assumption stand in for a decision. You spot the major developments and the roadblocks early, while there is still time to do something about them, and you put them in front of the Senior Project Manager and into the steering committee rather than discovering them in test.
 When you raise something, you bring the way through it. You prepare the discussion with the customer, make the implications clear in their language, and come with options. "We cannot do that and we will miss the go-live" is not the job. Working out what would make it possible, and what it costs, is. Where something exceeds the standard you prepare the decision rather than take it alone: options, effort, consequences, and a clear recommendation for the steering committee or for our engineering leadership.
 You are the strong technical counterpart for the customer's IT organization and for the Senior Project Manager. Both rely on you to know what is actually true. You work primarily up to the first go-live, where the solution design is either right or expensive, and you are staffed by process and landscape complexity rather than by deal size.
 A word on what you build. Our integration layer works like an iPaaS: connections are assembled as configuration on our own platform, specific to that customer, rather than written as code. You work in that layer yourself, so this is a hands-on role, and you document what you have configured so that the next person can understand and maintain it. What you do not do is write code that ships with the product. That distinction is what keeps a customer-specific solution from quietly becoming everyone's problem.
 Two roles sit either side of you and the handoffs are clean.
 With the Integrations Engineer: you define what the connection has to do and why, they build and operate it at that customer and own whether it runs. You hand them a specification, they come back with questions and constraints from the real system, and you resolve them together. When something breaks in their environment, it is theirs. When something is wrong in what was asked for, it is yours.
 With the Product Engineer: when a requirement cannot be met in configuration, or when the same requirement has now appeared at the third customer, you make the case for building it into the product. You write the specification, they build it, and you are the one who confirms it actually solves the customer problem it came from. After that it is part of the standard and you configure against it like anything else.

jobs.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager - EMEA
jobs.description:
Camunda is the enterprise platform for agentic orchestration , enabling organizations to coordinate AI agents, people, and systems across complex, end-to-end business processes. With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. Trusted by over 700 organizations worldwide , including 9 of top 10 US banks, Camunda helps enterprises boost operational efficiency, accelerate time-to-value, and deliver better customer experiences.

 Fully remote and global, we are in the middle of something bigger: transforming into an AI-first organisation, built on our own platform . We use Agentic AI to automate, orchestrate intelligent processes, and elevate human contribution across every team.

Named GP Bullhound’s Top 100 Next Unicorn list, 2025 Great Place to Work certified. Visionary in 2025 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Business Orchestration and Automation Technologies. ranked 3rd in Flexa's 2026 Most Flexible Companies , We’re growing fast and looking for top talent to join our team. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading. 
 
 About the Role: 
 Hi there! We're hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager to join our Product Marketing team.
 We're a group that cares about getting the story right, not just getting it out the door. We work closely with product, sales, and demand gen, and we hold ourselves to a high bar because our work directly shapes how the market understands what we build.
 This role gives you real ownership. You'll shape positioning and messaging for a meaningful piece of our product portfolio, build the competitive intelligence that keeps our field teams sharp, and work directly with sales leaders who depend on your materials to close deals. It's a role with visible impact, not one where your work disappears into a shared drive.
 As a Senior Product Marketing Manager, you'll drive go-to-market strategy for your area, from positioning through launch through enablement, while partnering with product and sales to make sure the message actually lands. This role matters because clear, credible product marketing is what turns a strong platform into a business result. Camunda operates in a technical, complex space, and getting that translation right is not optional.
 What You Will Do 
 Own positioning and messaging for your product area, translating technical capability into a clear value proposition for both technical and business buyers.

 Build and maintain a competitive intelligence program that sales actually uses, not just battlecards that sit in a folder.

 Lead go-to-market execution for launches in your area, coordinating across product, sales, and demand gen so the message is consistent everywhere it shows up.

 Arm the field with content that works in real conversations: pitch decks, demos, solution briefs, and objection handling.

 Use market and customer research to inform product and positioning decisions, not just to validate ones already made.

 Mentor and support other marketers on your team, sharing what you've learned without being asked.

 What You Will Bring to the Role 
 Significant experience in B2B product marketing, ideally in enterprise software, with a track record of owning positioning and messaging end to end, not just contributing pieces of it.

 A real competitive intelligence practice under your belt. You've built and maintained a program that sales relied on, not just responded to research requests as they came in.

 Comfort marketing technical products to technical buyers. You can go deep enough into a technical concept to be credible with a developer, and simplify it enough to be clear to an executive.

 Field enablement experience at scale. You've built programs that changed how a sales team talked about a product, and you know how to tell if it worked.

 Strong cross-functional instincts. You know how to build trust with product and sales without relying on authority, and how to bring people along on a positioning decision rather than just announcing it.

 Comfort using AI tools in your day to day work. This isn't a checkbox, it's part of how the role actually operates.

jobs.description:

Au cœur de l'écosystème digital de Decathlon, l'équipe Decathlon App fait le pont entre nos expériences e-commerce et le commerce physique. Notre mission dépasse la simple transaction : nous construisons un compagnon sportif quotidien, personnalisé et enrichi pour accompagner des millions d'utilisateur·ices dans leur pratique. Rejoindre notre équipe produit globale (iOS & Android), c'est évoluer dans un environnement stimulant où l'autonomie, l'impact à grande échelle et l'excellence méthodologique sont au cœur de nos défis quotidiens.

TA FUTURE CONTRIBUTION

En tant que Staff Product Manager (f/m/d), tu apporteras la vision stratégique et l'architecture fonctionnelle nécessaires pour faire passer notre application mobile à l'échelle supérieure. Tu opéreras avec une grande autonomie sur des enjeux complexes pour transformer l'expérience Decathlon App et garantir la cohérence de l'écosystème.

Tes responsabilités s'articulent autour de 4 piliers stratégiques :

  • Alignement stratégique, gestion des parties prenantes & vision app
    • Piloter la valeur globale (macro view) générée par les initiatives mobiles clés sur l'ensemble de l'écosystème business et client, au-delà des backlogs d'équipes individuelles.
    • Porter la vision produit auprès de la direction exécutive, des leaders business et des parties prenantes transversales pour aligner l'organisation sur la roadmap de l'application.
    • Définir les orientations stratégiques sur les segments utilisateurs prioritaires sur les points de contact mobiles natifs.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
Weekly office requirement: Monday/Wednesday weekly
Employment type: Permanent
Seniority level: Mid-senior

At GWI we’re always looking for extraordinary people who thrive on making an extraordinary impact. Right now we’re looking for a Product Manager to play a key role in our User Management (Revenue & Enablement) team in London. If that’s you, and making a difference gets you out of bed in the morning, keep reading. It could be the start of something, well, extraordinary.


Sounds great, what will I be doing? 🤔

As our Product Manager you'll own the systems that make GWI's subscription and consumption business run, such as billing, metering, user plans, feature access, product analytics and user messaging. It's the layer everything else sits on. Get it right and GWI can price, package and sell in new ways.


Two big pieces of work sit at the heart of this role. The first is billing for our consumption products, which is an area we're actively developing, and one you'll help shape. The second is making our internal tools talk to each other properly, so user data flows consistently between them and Salesforce, and everyone across the business is working from the same picture. Most of your stakeholders are internal - Revenue Operations, Finance, Business Intelligence, Client Success and Engineering - with some direct client contact along the way. You'll lead one squad of front-end and back-end engineers and a designer, alongside the PM and Engineers in our sister squad, Identity & Access - together you cover the whole of User Management.


A few things you’ll be responsible for: 


👉 Connecting our internal user management tools with Salesforce and each other, so data flows consistently and user information is mapped the same way everywhere

👉 Billing for our consumption products - metering, API usage, payment flows and user plans

👉 Customer feature flags, access and management - who can see what, and why

👉 Product analytics - event firing, sign-up flow data, usage data - so the business can see what's happening and act on it

👉 Building the roadmap from client feedback, internal stakeholder input and usage analytics, and prioritising the most valuable work

👉 Scoping the work and owning how your squad delivers it

It’s also fun; shaking things up is what working for GWI is all about. You’ll need to be flexible, comfortable with continuous change, and working in a high-tempo environment.


What do I need to bring with me? 🧳

You’ll need to be able to demonstrate the core skills this role requires. You don't have to tick all the boxes right away; the important thing is that you’re willing to learn. Here’s what the team will be looking for in you:


👉 You've shipped products at a B2B company

👉 You've built complex roadmaps with cross-functional dependencies, and you can balance multiple priorities without losing the plot

👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn't complete

👉 You're a strong problem solver, negotiator and influencer — you get alignment without needing authority

👉 You explain complex things clearly to very different audiences: execs, engineers, customers

👉 You ask questions and draw knowledge out of your team to find the right engineering and design solutions

👉 You make informed decisions at pace, even when the picture isn't complete, and you're happy taking a big initiative and running with it

👉 Bonus points if you've worked with Salesforce before, or with tools that need to sync data between systems and internal user management systems.
